title: 💀 Rockstar Says GTA VI Secrets Are Under Attack
description: Rockstar has revealed that hackers and even drones have been used in attempts to obtain information about GTA VI during development.
article_content:
Keeping Grand Theft Auto VI secret has become an enormous security challenge for Rockstar Games.

During an ongoing employment tribunal, Rockstar revealed that the company has faced serious attempts to obtain confidential GTA VI information. The studio said drones were used to try to photograph development activity through office windows, forcing Rockstar to install privacy film on some buildings.

Rockstar also revealed that a hacking group recently attempted to blackmail the company. The revelations show just how aggressively people are trying to obtain unreleased GTA VI information before launch.

Rockstar continues to maintain strict security measures around the game as development approaches its November release.

title: ❤️ Rockstar Wants GTA VI Fans to Love Jason & Lucia
description: Rockstar says it wants players to develop an emotional connection with Jason and Lucia similar to the bond fans formed with Arthur Morgan.
article_content:
Rockstar Games is aiming to make Jason and Lucia more emotionally memorable than previous GTA protagonists.

Rockstar North co-studio head Rob Nelson explained that the team wants players to develop a strong emotional connection with the two protagonists, similar to the relationship players formed with Arthur Morgan in Red Dead Redemption 2.

The developers are focusing not only on major missions and action but also on quieter moments between Jason and Lucia. These interactions are designed to make players understand their relationship and care about what happens to them throughout the story.

Rockstar hopes this deeper character focus will give GTA VI a more emotionally impactful story while still keeping the crime and action that define Grand Theft Auto.

description: Miami Beach commissioners voted 4-3 to approve a GTA VI promotional partnership that could bring around $3 million to the city.
